reason: The text explicitly depicts the Hebrew people complaining against their leader Moses. The passage shows: (1) the people quarreling/contending with Moses (וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם־ מֹשֶׁה); (2) demanding water (תְּנוּ־ לָנוּ מַיִם); (3) the people murmuring/complaining against Moses (וַיָּלֶן הָעָם עַל־ מֹשֶׁה); and (4) directly accusing him: 'Why have you brought us up from Egypt to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?' The location is subsequently named Massah (מַסָּה - testing) and Meribah (מְרִיבָה - contention/quarreling) specifically because of the people's strife with the Israelites and their testing of the LORD.
